transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Rivera, thank you for meeting with me. I want to talk to you about how your surgery went yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is everything okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There is something I need to tell you. During the procedure, a small metal clip was placed on the wrong structure inside your abdomen. This was a medical error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The clip is used to close off a vessel, but it was placed on a tissue it shouldn't have been on. We caught the mistake while you were still asleep in the operating room and we corrected it right then, but it required us to perform an additional procedure to fix it and make sure everything was safe.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just thought maybe the surgery was just harder than you expected because of my condition.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand why you might think that, but this wasn't due to your illness or the complexity of your anatomy. This was a mistake made by the surgical team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry this happened. I take full responsibility for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I mean, if it's fixed now, then it's fine. I don't want to cause any trouble.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're hesitant to push this, and I want you to know that speaking up about this isn't causing any trouble. It is my job to be honest with you about your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't want any problems with the hospital. Or anywhere else.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear your concern about your situation. I want to be very clear: this conversation is about your clinical care. Reporting this error is a medical requirement for us, and it does not change your status or how we provide your care here. You are safe here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure I've explained this clearly. In your own words, what is your understanding of what happened during the surgery?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You put a clip in the wrong spot and then had to do more work to move it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. It didn't cause any permanent damage, but it did extend the time you were under anesthesia. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. It makes sense.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to take in. I can see you're thinking about this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just didn't think this kind of thing happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It shouldn't happen. I realize this is unsettling and probably makes you feel uneasy about the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just glad it's over.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, I want to walk you through exactly what happens next so we can monitor your recovery. First, I am going to order an ultrasound for tomorrow morning at 9:00 AM to double-check that the area is healing exactly as it should.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will that cost more?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to handle the billing for that specific scan since it's related to the error. You won't be responsible for that charge. Second, I want you to track your pain levels on this chart every four hours. If you see a spike in pain, I need you to press the call button immediately so we can assess it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are also conducting a formal review of the surgical logs from yesterday. This is part of our quality system to figure out why the clip was misplaced so we can prevent this from happening to any other patient in the future.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I didn't know you did that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We do. It's the only way we can get better. I'll be back tomorrow morning after the ultrasound to go over the results with you. Do you have any questions for me right now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. I think I'm okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm going to leave you to rest for a bit. But please, if you think of anything later, or if you feel any anxiety about this, I want you to tell me. I am here for you.

H.justification: Resident allows full pauses, never interrupts, and maintains a regulated pace without any rushing language.

E.justification: Error named explicitly in the second turn, used lay language, and checked comprehension twice (teach-back and 'does that make sense').

A.justification: Direct apology used ('I am very sorry'), took full responsibility, and maintained accountability when the patient tried to downplay the error.

R.justification: Named specific emotions ('hesitant', 'unsettling', 'uneasy') and engaged with the patient's concerns about their status at the hospital.

T.justification: Provided specific steps (ultrasound tomorrow at 9am, pain tracking every 4 hours), defined the patient's role, and addressed prevention via the formal review.
